quizName: Hardest Questions in Rhode island Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Having a passenger on your motorcycle:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Helps new riders practice different situations.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can make you move into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make you move into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and try to stay awake.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to avoid getting tired.

questions.question: A friend has drunk too much alcohol and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk alcohol to ride. Stop them any way you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: What best reduces the risk of head and neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Provide the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your whole face. A face shield is better because it protects your entire face. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before your first ride. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes long pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: To check your tire pressure, you should:
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. Looking at the tire is not enough because an under-inflated tire may still look normal.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you better, even in the daytime.

questions.question: Why are motorcycle turn signals important?

options.text: They are not very important since motorcycles are small.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
You should skip them if no vehicles are nearby.
They work differently than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more at risk. Always use your turn signals to warn others when you plan to turn or change lanes—even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Why should you wear a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It is too warm to wear in hot weather.
It protects you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is around.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves?

options.text: They make it harder to control your motorcycle and should be avoided.
They help other drivers see you.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: How does your body get rid of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your body can only remove alcohol through time. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: What type of helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
One that survived a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Which organization certifies motorcycle helmets for safety?
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet certified by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for maximum protection.

questions.question: Wet and loose surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates in the road. Ride slowly and carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source for information. It has details about how your motorcycle works, its specifications, and recommended maintenance.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is controlled by twisting the right hand grip.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle you are not familiar with, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding, learn how it works. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Find the gear pattern. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider be seen better by other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors with reflective materials. Always use your headlight. Use your turn signals and brake light properly. This helps other drivers see you.
